note: Instruction to a colleague organising churches in Crete: leaders, households, the teaching of grace, and good works. Not cited by the curriculum or the Scriptural Appendix.
coverage_note: 1:1-4 and 1:10-14 (including the quotation 'Cretans are always liars') are not indexed. 2:1-10 is indexed with the household-code guard stated in the entry.

entries.pericope: The overseer must be blameless, as God's steward; not self-pleasing, not easily angered… but given to hospitality, a lover of good, sober minded, fair
entries.connection: The same pattern as 1 Timothy 3: leaders chosen by character tested in the household. 'For the overseer must be blameless, as God's steward; not self-pleasing, not easily angered, not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for dishonest gain; but given to hospitality, a lover of good, sober minded, fair, holy, self-controlled.' C08's teacher known by the life, and C14's home as the proving ground.

entries.pericope: To the pure, all things are pure… They profess that they know God, but by their works they deny him
entries.connection: 'To the pure, all things are pure; but to those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure; but both their mind and their conscience are defiled.' C07's lens: what one sees depends on the condition of the eye. And C12's proof stated as an accusation: 'They profess that they know God, but by their works they deny him.' The quotation about Cretans at 1:12-13 is not indexed.

entries.pericope: That older women likewise be… teachers of that which is good… in all things showing yourself an example of good works… that they may adorn the doctrine of God
entries.connection: Instruction by age and station: older men 'temperate, sensible… sound in faith, in love, and in patience'; older women 'teachers of that which is good,' training the younger; Titus himself 'in all things showing yourself an example of good works.' C05's apprenticeship through every generation of the household, C14. The stated aim throughout is the witness to outsiders — 'that God's word may not be blasphemed'; 'that he who opposes you may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say about us'; 'that they may adorn the doctrine' — C17. Indexed with the household-code guard used elsewhere: the instructions to wives and slaves are recorded as first-century household structures addressed for the sake of witness, and the index anchors the mentoring and the example, not the hierarchy.

entries.pericope: The grace of God has appeared… instructing us to the intent that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we would live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present world
entries.connection: 'For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all men, instructing us…' Grace as teacher rather than permission — C19's mercy producing C26's change: 'denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we would live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present world.' A people purified 'for his own possession, zealous for good works.'

entries.pericope: To speak evil of no one, not to be contentious, to be gentle, showing all humility toward all men. For we were also once foolish, disobedient, deceived
entries.connection: 'Remind them to be in subjection to rulers and to authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work, to speak evil of no one, not to be contentious, to be gentle, showing all humility toward all men.' The Citizen-Stranger's ordinary goodness and its refusal of contempt toward outsiders (medium). Then the reason, which is Self-Accusation: 'For we were also once foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving various lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.' Remember your own past before you speak evil of anyone else's present (medium). And C19's door: 'But when the kindness of God our Savior and his love toward mankind appeared, not by works of righteousness, which we did ourselves, but according to his mercy, he saved us.'

entries.pericope: Be careful to maintain good works… Avoid a factious man after a first and second warning… Let our people also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses
entries.connection: 'Those who have believed God may be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable to men; but shun foolish questionings… strife, and disputes about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.' C12's proof and C15's peace: argument is not the work. 'Avoid a factious man after a first and second warning' — patience with a limit. And the letter's practical close: 'Send Zenas, the lawyer, and Apollos on their journey speedily, that nothing may be lacking for them. Let our people also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they may not be unfruitful.' C13's good works aimed at actual need.
